description: The cross-company reverse-split lists the Signal8 Reverse Splits page serves, one view per call. view "upcoming" = splits with an effective date from tomorrow through 30 US market days ahead, the vendor market calendar union Signal8's SEC-filing tracker (filings, exchange and depositary notices); "recent" = the same union for effective dates in the past 30 days; "approved_no_date" = tracked episodes where shareholders (or the board, where no vote is required) have approved a reverse split but no effective date is stated yet; "vote_pending" = tracked episodes where a reverse split is proposed and the shareholder vote has not happened yet; "cancelled" = tracked episodes that ended without the split taking effect in the past 90 days (withdrawn by the company, a vote that did not approve it, an approved authority that expired unused, a meeting postponed indefinitely), with a cancelled object (outcome, outcomeLabel, endedOn, endedOnBasis, laterEpisode when the company has a newer open proposal) and the closing document as the source; older ended episodes are on the separate ended-reverse-splits tool. A security sits on exactly one of the first four views (upcoming, then recent, then approved_no_date, then vote_pending), with one exception: a split the company's own filing dates is on upcoming even when the same company also has a different, later split proposal awaiting a vote, which is then on vote_pending too; "cancelled" may repeat a company another view lists. Each row carries ticker, companyName, hasPage, source ("market_calendar" or "tracker"), stage + stageLabel, trackerState, ratio (or ratioMin / ratioMax for an authorised range), meetingDate, approvedDate, effectiveDate, effectiveDateSource, marketCalendarAgrees / marketCalendarDate / marketCalendarRatio, effectiveCondition, verification, marketConfirmation (recent only), marketCapUsd + capBucket, securityType, exchange, cik, sourceUrl / sourceAccession / sourceFormType / sourceFiledDate / sourceLabel, sourceDocuments (every document behind the episode), quote, adsRatioChange, approvalPath, domicile, splitAuthority and authorityTerms. Null means not measured or not stated: not "no split", not zero, not "no vote needed" and not "no date". A null ratio = the documents state none yet; a null marketCapUsd = cap not measured (capBucket is then null, not "nano"); a null verification = no tracked episode; a null domicile = not measured (not "Delaware"); a null marketConfirmation = the price step was not measured. An empty rows array on a view is normal and is not evidence that no company is splitting. completeness says what the view is: "scheduled_as_of_now" (upcoming) and "recorded_as_of_now" (recent) are what is known as of now, not "all reverse splits"; "tracked_episodes" is what the tracker has read from filings since it started, not every company. A scheduled split can still be postponed or cancelled: it is scheduled, not confirmed. Dates: effectiveDate is the scheduled effective date (vendor calendar, or the issuer-stated date strictly parsed from the filing); a filing or listing-rule deadline is not an effective date and does not appear in this field. A conditional date ("the 25th trading day after...") is returned verbatim in effectiveCondition and is not a date. effectiveDateSource says where effectiveDate came from: "filing" = the issuer stated it; "market_calendar" = the filing states no date and the vendor calendar supplies it. marketCalendarAgrees is a cross-check on a tracker row the calendar also lists: true = same date and ratio; false = at least one differs and marketCalendarDate / marketCalendarRatio hold the calendar's value (the filing's value is the row's value, and the two sources disagree); null or absent = not compared (no calendar row). meetingDate is the shareholder meeting date, not the split date. Approval and authority: approvalPath.path is shareholder_vote, written_consent, fpi_written_resolution, pre_approved_range (the board sets the ratio inside a range shareholders approved earlier), board_only (the issuer's own filing says no shareholder approval is required, quoted), depositary_ratio_change (an ADS ratio change by the depositary, no vote) or unknown ("Not determined", not "no vote"). splitAuthority.boardMayActWithoutVote is true only from the issuer's own filing or charter; a domicile default alone is not a finding. authorityTerms is the authority behind the episode: a cumulativeCap (the board may split in steps, each within the cap, without a new vote until the authority expires), multiStep, the expiry, and what executed splits already used; null = the documents state nothing beyond the ratio. Locked rows are withheld, not absent. The split facts on every view are part of Signal8 Pro. A caller whose API key is not owned by a Pro account gets every row with locked: true and only ticker, companyName, hasPage and exchange on it; the response then carries access: "preview", lockedCount (how many rows are locked) and rowLimit. A locked row means the facts exist and were not shown to this caller (they need Signal8 Pro); it does not mean "no split". access: "full" = every row carries its facts. filtersLimitedToUnlocked: true = a board / domicile filter was applied to unlocked rows only (locked rows are left out entirely, because matching them would reveal the fact through membership). Filters apply server-side: cap (scanner buckets), type (security type), exchange, board ("without_vote": board split authority on file, from the issuer's own filing or charter) and domicile. Each accepts "not_measured" to select rows where that fact was not measured; an unmeasured row never matches a measured bucket. totalCount is the filtered list (locked rows included), unfilteredCount the view before filters, capUnknownCount the rows whose cap was not measured (on the calendar views). Paging uses limit / offset; truncated: true = more rows exist. available: false with reason "tracker_not_enabled" (the three tracker views) means the tracker is switched off, not that nothing is pending. An HTTP 503 FEATURE_DISABLED means the page is switched off, and the response then says nothing about any company's split. The data describes what is on file and carries no view on whether a split will happen, what it means for the price, or what anyone should do.

board.description: ["without_vote"] keeps only rows whose issuer can split without a shareholder vote on the evidence of its OWN filing or charter (a domicile default never matches). Pro-only fact: on a non-Pro key it applies to unlocked rows only.

cap.description: Market-cap buckets to keep (the premarket scanner's): nano, micro, small, mid, large, or not_measured for rows whose cap was not measured. Empty = every row.

domicile.description: Registrant domicile groups to keep: bvi, nevada, cayman, marshall_islands, bermuda, delaware, other, or not_measured. Pro-only fact: on a non-Pro key it applies to unlocked rows only.

exchange.description: Listing venues to keep: NASDAQ, NYSE, AMEX (NYSE American), OTC, or not_measured. Empty = every row.

offset.description: Rows to skip (default 0). Locked rows count towards paging.

type.description: Security types to keep: common, adr (ADR / ADS), ordinary (foreign ordinary shares), other, or not_measured. Empty = every row.

view.description: Which list: "upcoming" (effective tomorrow through 30 market days ahead; the calendar UNION the tracker), "recent" (effective in the past 30 days), "approved_no_date" (approved, no effective date stated yet), "vote_pending" (proposed; the shareholder vote has not happened), "cancelled" (ended without taking effect in the past 90 days). Default "upcoming".
